summary: Design the agent quick-answer notification channel and Amanda tone/pacing doctrine, then adversarially review

channel.mechanism:
The agent's ticket alert IS a WhatsApp message from the agency's existing Twilio WhatsApp number, and the agent's answer IS a normal WhatsApp reply to it. When Amanda files an amanda_question ticket, the system sends the agent an approved utility template (required because the agent's 24h customer-service window is usually closed): "New client question — reply to this message to answer. Client: {{1}} ({{2}}) / Property: {{3}} — {{4}} / Question: \"{{5}}\" / Ticket Q{{6}} — reply with your answer, or CALL to take over." The agent long-presses the notification (iOS haptic-touch inline reply) or taps Reply on the Android notification and types the answer — this is exactly the founder's dream interaction, with one verified caveat: notification inline-reply sends a PLAIN message, not a WhatsApp quote-reply, so ticket matching must be a deterministic ladder, not quote-context alone. The inbound reply hits the existing Twilio webhook; a new router branch checks the From number against an agency_staff_numbers table BEFORE the lead pipeline (staff numbers never create leads, never wake Amanda-the-seller). Matching ladder: (1) OriginalRepliedMessageSid present (agent quote-replied in-chat, or tapped a template quick-reply button — both verified to carry it, ≤7 days) → look up the SID in amanda_question_notifications → exact ticket; (2) ButtonPayload present → ticket id; (3) body starts with a short-code (regex ^(?:Q|#)?(\d{1,2})[:.\s-]) → that ticket; (4) exactly one open ticket for this agent → it; (5) multiple open tickets → send a numbered disambiguation menu (session message — free and unrestricted, because the agent's reply just opened their 24h window; optionally a twilio/list-picker, which is session-only by policy) and match the next reply.

The moment the agent's first reply lands, their 24h window is open, so everything after is free-form and free: the confirmation ("✓ Q3 answered. Amanda is telling María in Norwegian: '…' — reply UPDATE Q3 to correct, CALL to take over"), clarification loops, and any re-pings within 24h. Re-notification runs on a scheduler: T0 template ping → T+10min reminder (template again if window still closed) → T+30min escalate to the next staff number / the agency escalation phone → overdue flag on dashboard, all inside agency quiet hours (09:00–21:00 local, else queued). Reserved commands parsed deterministically first, LLM-intent fallback second (matching Amanda's existing deterministic-validators-plus-sonnet architecture): CALL/ME → full handoff (Amanda pauses on that conversation, tells the buyer the agent will contact them directly); NOT MINE → reassign; LATER → snooze 2h; UPDATE Qn → correct an already-relayed answer; LIST → list open tickets. Amanda relays the answer to the buyer in the buyer's language with attribution — as a free session message if the buyer's window is open (usual case, they just asked), else via a buyer-side utility template ("I checked with the office about {{2}}: {{3}}") in the buyer's language, reusing the existing 13-language template infrastructure.
details: VERIFIED PLATFORM FACTS (Twilio docs/changelog, checked 2026-08-26): inbound WhatsApp webhooks include OriginalRepliedMessageSid + OriginalRepliedMessageSender for quote-replies AND quick-reply button taps, only when the replied-to message is ≤7 days old (twilio.com/en-us/changelog/whatsapp-inbound-messages-will-now-include-reply-context); twilio/quick-reply: up to 10 buttons in an APPROVED template, only 3 buttons in a session message without approval, body max 1,024 chars, button title max 20 chars, taps return ButtonText + ButtonPayload (twilio.com/docs/content/twilio-quick-reply); twilio/list-picker is restricted to session (conversational) messages — it can NEVER be an approved template (twilio.com/docs/content/content-types-overview); cards and CTA-button types require approval even in-session.

CRITICAL UX truth: on both iOS (haptic-touch/long-press the notification → inline text field) and Android (Reply action on the notification), the inline reply is delivered as a PLAIN chat message — it does NOT set WhatsApp quote-reply context. Quote-reply (swipe-to-reply) only happens if the agent opens the chat. Therefore the matching ladder (SID → ButtonPayload → short-code → single-open-ticket → disambiguation) is the load-bearing design, and the single-open-ticket case (the overwhelmingly common one for a small agency) makes bare inline replies 'just work'.

TEMPLATE DESIGN (utility category — a notification about an existing service interaction, zero promotional content; no Meta policy problem with messaging your own opted-in staff, but explicit opt-in must be recorded at enrollment per WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy). Body obeys Meta rules: no variable at start or end, no adjacent variables, variable values must not contain newlines (strip/flatten the question text). Variables: {{1}} lead first name, {{2}} lead language label ('Norwegian'), {{3}} property ref (IC-28746), {{4}} property short title truncated ~40 chars, {{5}} question text truncated ~200 chars, {{6}} ticket short-code digit(s). Optional approved quick-reply buttons on the same template: [Take over chat] [Not mine] — even if button payloads are static, OriginalRepliedMessageSid on the tap identifies the ticket. Submit only in the languages agency STAFF actually speak (ES/EN first), not all 13.

INBOUND ROUTER SEGREGATION: new table agency_staff_numbers(id, agency_id, phone_e164, display_name, role, priority, locale, verified_at, opt_in_at, opt_in_message_sid, last_inbound_at, active) with uniqueness per (agency_id, phone_e164). Router precedence, keyed multi-tenant-safe: resolve agency from the To (Twilio sender) number first, THEN check From against that agency's staff table — staff hit routes to the ticket handler and hard-stops the lead pipeline (no lead creation, no Amanda-seller, no interest-capture triggers). Same phone can legitimately be a buyer at a different agency because the key is (agency, phone).

TICKET DATA MODEL: amanda_questions(id, agency_id, short_code, lead_id, conversation_id, property_id, question_text, question_lang, status: open|clarifying|answered|handoff|reassigned|expired|cancelled, assigned_staff_id, answer_text, answered_at, relay_message_sid, created_at) + amanda_question_notifications(id, ticket_id, staff_id, message_sid, channel: template|session, kind: initial|reminder|escalation|disambiguation|confirmation, sent_at). Every outbound ping's Twilio Message SID is stored so ladder step 1 is a single indexed lookup. Short-codes are allocated per agent as the smallest unused integer among that agent's open tickets (so they stay Q1–Q9 in practice) and are recycled only after close.

24H WINDOW STATE MACHINE (agent side): last_inbound_at on the staff row tracks the window. Send free-form session messages when now − last_inbound_at < 24h (richer, multi-line, free); otherwise send the approved utility template. Safety net: if a free-form send fails with Twilio error 63016 (out-of-window), auto-fall back to the template. Utility templates delivered inside an open customer-service window are free under Meta's per-message pricing (in force since July 2025); outside the window a utility template in Spain costs on the order of €0.02–0.04 + Twilio's ~$0.005 per-message fee — pennies per ticket, verify current rate card at build time.

RE-NOTIFICATION SCHEDULE (configurable per agency): T0 initial template → T+10min reminder → T+30min escalation to next priority staff number or the agency's existing escalation phone → T+60min mark overdue on dashboard + Amanda manages buyer expectations ('the office will confirm — meanwhile, may I show you two similar villas?'). All pings respect agency-local quiet hours 09:00–21:00 (queued otherwise). Reminders reuse the SAME approved template (allowed) with the same variables; scheduler = a per-minute tick in the existing Railway API worker (the 30-min calendar sweep cadence is too coarse for this).

DISAMBIGUATION (ladder step 5): reply is a numbered text menu — 'Which question is this answer for? 1️⃣ Q3 · María · IC-28746 · price negotiable? 2️⃣ Q5 · Jonas · IC-30112 · pets allowed? Reply with the number, or resend as "Q3: your answer".' Sent as a session message (free — the agent's reply just opened the window). Optional polish: twilio/list-picker rows for the same choices (session-only type, verified). The agent's next message is matched to the menu; a short-code prefix always overrides everything.

CONFIRMATION LOOP: after relay, agent gets '✓ Q3 answered. Amanda is telling María (in Norwegian): "Yes — the owner will consider offers around 5% below asking." Reply UPDATE Q3 to correct, or CALL to take over.' Echoing Amanda's actual outgoing phrasing gives the agent implicit verification of both translation and content. A deterministic quality gate runs BEFORE relay: empty/emoji-only/unusable answers, or an answer that is itself a question ('which María?'), flips the ticket to status=clarifying and Amanda-agent-side replies with the missing context instead of relaying junk to the buyer.

RESERVED COMMANDS (deterministic regex first, LLM intent classification fallback for natural phrasings like 'I'll just call her' — consistent with the locked Amanda architecture of deterministic validators around the sonnet loop): CALL or ME → convert to full handoff (pause Amanda on that conversation, notify buyer in their language that the agent will contact them directly, create handoff task); NOT MINE / SKIP → reassign to next staff by priority; LATER → snooze re-pings 2h; UPDATE Qn → replace an already-relayed answer (Amanda sends a graceful correction to the buyer); LIST → list this agent's open tickets. Parse commands in the agent's locale synonyms too (LLAMAR, MÍA, LUEGO).

ENROLLMENT (smallest-lovable): dashboard Settings → Team → 'Add agent WhatsApp': enter E.164 → system sends a verification template with a 6-digit code → agent replies with the code. That single reply (a) proves number ownership, (b) is the recorded WhatsApp opt-in (store timestamp + Message SID), (c) proves the number actually has WhatsApp (Twilio error 63003 if not), and (d) opens the first 24h window so the welcome/explainer message is free-form. Routing v1: property.assigned_agent_id if set, else the staff row with priority=1, else the existing escalation phone — no round-robin until an agency actually has enough agents to need it.

BUYER-SIDE RELAY: usual case is a free session message (buyer asked minutes ago). Attribution phrasing localized per language, SHORT by default per the founder's tone rule ('I checked with the office — yes, the owner would consider offers around 5% below.'). If the buyer's 24h window has lapsed by the time the answer arrives, send a new buyer-facing utility template answer_followup ('Hi {{1}}, I checked with the office about {{2}}: {{3}}') submitted in all 13 languages through the existing proven Twilio Content API pipeline. Amanda's engagement-while-waiting and richer-message-on-disengagement behavior is prompt/policy config in the existing agentic loop, not new infrastructure.

VOICE-NOTE ANSWERS (agents will do this in real life): inbound webhook carries MediaUrl0 + MediaContentType audio/ogg. v1: transcribe (hosted STT), run the same quality gate, and lean on the confirmation echo — the agent sees exactly what Amanda will say and can UPDATE if the transcription is wrong. v0 fallback if STT is out of scope: reply 'please type the answer for Q3'.
edge_cases: Inline notification reply is a bare message with no quote context (verified platform behavior) → handled by the matching ladder; with one open ticket (the normal case) it matches instantly; never assume OriginalRepliedMessageSid is present.
Multiple open tickets + bare reply → numbered disambiguation menu (session message, free); short-code prefix 'Q3: …' always bypasses it.

Agent quote-replies to a notification older than 7 days → Twilio drops the reply context (verified limit) → falls through to short-code / single-ticket / disambiguation; tickets should auto-expire well before 7 days anyway (default expire + dashboard-only at 48h).

Reply arrives for an already-answered or expired ticket → 'Q3 was already answered by [name] at 14:02 — reply UPDATE Q3 to change it.' First answer wins on a race between two staff numbers; the loser is notified.

Agent's answer is empty, unusable, or itself a question ('which María?') → quality gate flips ticket to clarifying; Amanda answers the agent with lead context and does NOT relay; re-ping schedule keeps running.

Agent replies STOP (Twilio Advanced Opt-Out applies to any recipient) → all pings to that number legally suppressed; detect the opt-out, alert the agency admin on the dashboard and route tickets to the next staff number; enrollment explainer pre-empts this ('reply LATER to snooze, don't block').

Template undeliverable — number has no WhatsApp (63003) or delivery fails → mark staff row undeliverable, escalate to next staff/escalation phone immediately, surface on dashboard; enrollment verification makes this rare after day one.

Staff number collides with an existing lead record in the SAME agency → staff table wins in the router; flag and quarantine the lead record so Amanda never re-engages it; cross-agency same-number is a non-issue because routing keys on (To→agency, From).

Agent deletes their WhatsApp answer ('delete for everyone') → Twilio sends no deletion webhook; if already relayed it cannot be unsent → UPDATE Qn is the correction path (Amanda sends a graceful correction to the buyer).

Buyer's 24h window closed before the answer arrived (agent slow, quiet hours) → buyer-side relay must switch from session message to the answer_followup utility template in the buyer's language, else the send fails with 63016.

Meta template quality rating drops (staff marking pings as spam would pause the template) → near-zero risk with opted-in staff, but monitor template quality status via the Content API and alert if paused; keep the copy strictly transactional so utility categorization is never challenged.
Quiet hours: ticket filed at 23:30 → buyer gets an honest 'I'll confirm with the office first thing tomorrow'; agent ping queued to 09:00 unless the agency opts into 24/7 pings.

GDPR: lead first name + question forwarded to an agent's personal phone via Meta → keep payload minimal (first name only, no phone/email in the template), record it in the agency DPA/processor chain — same legal lane as Christian's existing Amanda DPA blocker, flag for his legal review, not a build blocker.
channel.recommendation: Build this WhatsApp-native channel as the ticket notification mechanism — it is the correct call. It runs entirely on infrastructure AIVENA already owns (Twilio sender, Content API template pipeline proven across 13 languages, the inbound webhook, the Railway worker), it needs no PWA/push lane and no native app, and the verified notification-inline-reply behavior on both iOS and Android IS the founder's dream interaction. Build order: (1) agency_staff_numbers table + inbound router precedence branch with tests proving a staff reply can never create a lead or wake Amanda-the-seller — this is the safety-critical piece and everything else sits on it; (2) ticket + notification tables, short-code allocator, and the matching ladder; (3) the agent utility template (ES/EN) submitted via the existing Content API pipeline + the T0 send path; (4) confirmation loop + quality gate + CALL/NOT MINE/LATER/UPDATE commands; (5) re-ping scheduler with escalation and quiet hours; (6) disambiguation menu; (7) enrollment UI in Settings → Team with code verification-as-opt-in; (8) buyer-side answer_followup template in 13 languages; (9) polish: quick-reply buttons on the template, list-picker disambiguation, voice-note transcription. Ship 1–5 as the v1 gate (a single-agent agency gets the full dream loop); 6–9 follow. Explicitly write into the design doc that quote-reply is NOT required for matching — the ladder is — so nobody 'simplifies' it later into a broken assumption.
channel.build_cost: Roughly 2 developer-weeks for v1 (steps 1–5), all inside the existing Hono API + Supabase + Twilio stack: staff table + router branch with negative-path tests ~2 days; ticket model, SID-indexed notifications, matching ladder ~2–3 days; template authoring + Content API submission ~half a day of work plus Meta approval latency (typically minutes-to-hours per language via the pipeline already exercised for the 13-language set); confirmation/commands/quality gate ~2 days; re-ping scheduler ~1–2 days (needs a per-minute tick — the existing 30-min worker cadence is too coarse, so add a lightweight cron/queue in the Railway worker); enrollment UI ~1–2 days; buyer-side follow-up template in 13 languages ~1 day using the proven translation/audit flow. Voice-note transcription adds ~1–2 days plus an STT dependency. Running cost is negligible: one utility template ping ≈ €0.02–0.04 + ~$0.005 Twilio fee per message (per-message Meta pricing since July 2025 — verify the Spain rate card at build time), and everything after the agent's first reply is free inside the 24h window; a busy day of 20 tickets with reminders is well under €2. Hard dependencies: Meta approval of the agent template (low risk, transactional utility copy), recorded staff opt-in at enrollment (built into the flow), and the GDPR/DPA note for lead data on staff personal phones (Christian's existing legal lane, not an engineering blocker). No dependency on the PWA push lane whatsoever. Sources: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/whatsapp-inbound-messages-will-now-include-reply-context ; https://www.twilio.com/docs/content/twilio-quick-reply ; https://www.twilio.com/docs/content/content-types-overview

push.mechanism:
VERIFIED REALITY (2025-26). iOS: web push works only for a Home Screen web app (manifest display standalone/fullscreen, user must Share→Add to Home Screen in Safari, permission request must come from a tap) — iOS 16.4+, delivered via APNs (webkit.org/blog/13878). It DOES work in Spain/EU: Apple's Feb-2024 DMA removal only ever existed in iOS 17.4 betas and was fully reversed before release — standalone PWAs + push were restored and remain (9to5mac.com/2024/03/01, pushalert.co reversal post); ignore 2026 SEO blogs still claiming "no EU push". iOS plays the default sound, supports app icon badging (setAppBadge; declarative "app_badge" on 18.4+), respects Focus modes but can NEVER be Time-Sensitive or break through Focus (native-only entitlement), and WebKit supports NO notification action buttons and NO inline reply — a tap can only open a URL. Classic iOS web push also revokes the subscription after a few pushes that fail to show a notification; iOS/iPadOS 18.4's Declarative Web Push removes that penalty by making the payload itself renderable (webkit.org/blog/16535). Subscriptions still die silently in practice (device restarts, Safari data clearing) — re-validate on every app open. Android Chrome: full support, no install required, FCM-backed delivery with browser closed, action buttons, tag/renotify replacement — and the big verified surprise: NOTIFICATION INLINE TEXT REPLY SHIPPED TO STABLE (NotificationAction {type:"text"} + event.reply in notificationclick; chromestatus feature 5743740178137088: "Enabled by default", Android since Chrome 68, desktop since 75; iOS: not supported). So the founder's dream — expand notification, type the answer inline, send — is REAL on Android web push and on desktop Chrome/Edge, and impossible on iPhone via web push in any form.

CORE MECHANISM: when Amanda files an amanda_question ticket, the Hono API fans out an encrypted Web Push (VAPID, web-push npm lib, Urgency:high, TTL≈30min) to every registered device subscription of the assigned agent(s), stored per-device in Postgres. The service worker shows a notification built for 2-second lock-screen comprehension (buyer+language+property in title, verbatim translated question as body), tagged q-<ticketId>. Tap → clients.openWindow("/dashboard/questions/<id>") → a pre-focused one-box Answer Composer. On Android/desktop an "Answer" text action lets the agent type the reply inside the notification; the SW POSTs it with a per-ticket one-time signed token embedded in the (end-to-end-encrypted) push payload. Unanswered tickets re-ping on a ladder (same tag + renotify:true so it re-alerts instead of stacking). On answer, a low-priority "resolve" push makes each device's SW close/replace the stale notification by tag (remote dismissal IS possible this way on Android/desktop; on iOS every push must display something, so the resolve push is skipped or replaced with a quiet "Answered ✓" + badge clear).
details: Notification content pattern (2-second rule): title = '❓ {BuyerFirstName} {flag/lang} · {PropertyShortName} · {price}' e.g. '❓ Marta (DE) · Villa Alegría · 289k€'; body = the buyer's question verbatim, pre-translated by Amanda into the agency's language, in quotes: '"Is the price negotiable?"'; icon = agency logo, badge = monochrome AIVENA glyph (Android status bar), tag = 'q-<ticketId>', data = {url, ticketId, answerToken}.

Android/desktop actions: actions:[{action:'answer', type:'text', title:'Responder', placeholder:'Escribe la respuesta…'},{action:'open', title:'Abrir'}]; in notificationclick, event.action==='answer' reads event.reply and POSTs /tickets/:id/answer with the one-time token via event.waitUntil(fetch...); on success show a self-replacing '✓ Enviado a Marta' notification (same tag); on network failure fall back to opening the composer with the text preserved. Feature-detect: iOS ignores unknown 'actions' harmlessly, so ONE payload serves all platforms.

Answer Composer /dashboard/questions/[id]: header row = buyer name + language flag + 'via WhatsApp', property card (thumbnail, ref, town, price — one line), the question in a quote bubble, optional grey line of what Amanda already told the buyer, ONE autofocused textarea, one Send button. After send: '✓ Amanda is delivering this in German'. States: already-answered (show answer + who + when, composer hidden), ticket-cancelled (buyer got answer another way), unauthenticated (login with return_to deep link back to the ticket).

Subscriptions table push_subscriptions: id, user_id, agency_id, endpoint (unique), p256dh, auth, ua_platform, created_at, last_success_at, failure_count. One VAPID keypair for the whole product (keys in Railway env). Endpoints: POST /push/subscriptions (upsert on endpoint), DELETE. Client re-validates on every dashboard load: pushManager.getSubscription(); null or changed → resubscribe + upsert (this is the only workable answer to iOS killing subscriptions silently).

Pruning: web-push sendNotification rejecting with 404/410 → delete row immediately; also sweep failure_count>5 or last_success_at>90d. This is the standard, reliable mechanism — there is no API to query whether an iOS subscription is still alive.

Re-notification ladder (per-agency configurable, stop on answer/claim): T0 ping → T+3min → T+10min (renotify:true re-alerts the SAME notification, no stacking) → T+20min escalate to backup agent/office number → T+40min notify admin. Web push headers: Urgency:'high', TTL 1800s so a stale ping never lands hours late; the resolve push gets TTL 86400.

Remote dismissal (verified possible on Android/desktop): resolve push → SW does registration.getNotifications({tag:'q-<id>'}) → .close(); to stay within Chrome's must-show-a-notification rule, replace with silent 'Answered ✓' same-tag notification that a second step may close, or simply let the silent replacement sit. iOS: skip resolve pushes on classic web push (silent handling risks subscription revocation) until the fleet is on 18.4+ Declarative Web Push, where a mutable low-key replacement + app_badge:0 is safe.

Per-device double-ping suppression: in the push handler, clients.matchAll({type:'window',includeUncontrolled:true}) — if a focused dashboard window exists on THAT device, skip showNotification and fire an in-app toast instead. Cross-device (phone+desktop both subscribed): deliberately DO double-deliver; the resolve push cleans both. Cross-CHANNEL: since the escalation phone already gets a WhatsApp template, default policy = WhatsApp is the phone ping, web push always goes to desktop-class subscriptions, and mobile web-push delivery is a per-agent toggle (default on only for Android agents who want inline reply).

Security of inline reply: the answerToken is a short-lived (ladder-lifetime) JWT scoped to one ticket, embedded in the push payload — web push payloads are end-to-end encrypted (RFC 8291), the push services never see plaintext; POST is idempotent and race-guarded (answered_at IS NULL).

iOS install UX must be built, not assumed: a guided 'Get notifications on iPhone' sheet (Share → Add to Home Screen → open the icon → tap Enable) with detection of standalone mode (matchMedia display-mode) and Notification.permission; once a user taps 'Don't Allow' it can only be fixed in iOS Settings — say so on screen.

What this pulls forward from the PWA lane: manifest.json + icons, the service worker, install/standalone detection, and the add-to-home-screen education UX. It does NOT need offline caching, background sync, or the app-shell work — those stay in the later lane; the SW file just gains push/notificationclick handlers now.

Payload budget: web push allows ~4KB encrypted payload — question text + property line + token fit comfortably; truncate question at ~180 chars for the notification body, full text lives on the composer.

Focus-mode truth for the doc: Home Screen web apps appear as first-class apps in iOS notification/Focus settings, so agents CAN allow-list AIVENA in a work Focus — but nothing in web push can force through an unconfigured Focus or Do Not Disturb, on either platform. WhatsApp has exactly the same constraint, but agents have usually already allow-listed WhatsApp.
edge_cases: iOS subscription silently dead (restart, Safari data clearing, iOS housekeeping): unrecoverable server-side; handled by resubscribe-on-every-open plus 410-pruning, and by WhatsApp remaining the guaranteed channel — never rely on iOS web push alone for must-ping.

Agent denied notification permission on iOS: permanent until changed in Settings → app shows a persistent yellow 'notifications off' banner with the exact Settings path; server marks the agent web-push-unreachable so the ladder goes straight to WhatsApp/backup.
Two agents notified, both answer: first POST wins via answered_at IS NULL guard; loser gets 200-with-state 'already answered by X' and their notification is resolved-dismissed.

Answer typed inline on Android with no connectivity (agent in a garage): SW fetch fails → openWindow to composer with the text passed through (and composer drafts persist in localStorage); do not silently drop a typed answer.

Ticket answered seconds before a scheduled re-ping fires: ladder job re-checks status at send time AND TTL 1800 means an undelivered stale ping expires at the push service instead of landing at midnight.
Quiet hours: buyer asks at 23:40 → Amanda tells the buyer the office answers in the morning, ticket queues, ladder starts at agency opening time (per-agency schedule, Europe/Madrid default).

Duplicate same-phone ping (agent has WhatsApp escalation AND installed the PWA on the same phone): per-agent channel matrix defaults mobile web push OFF when an escalation WhatsApp number is configured for that agent; toggle exposed in settings.
Locked Android phone: inline reply from lock screen depends on the user's lock-screen notification settings (may require unlock first) — works, but the doc must not promise zero-unlock in all cases.

Old iPhones / EU misinformation: iOS <16.4 has no web push at all (WhatsApp only); and any tester who reads that 'EU push is removed' should be pointed to the verified iOS 17.4-release reversal — it works in Spain today.

Push payload arrives but SW fails to render (JS error): classic iOS revokes the subscription after a few such failures — keep the push handler tiny and defensive (try/catch around JSON.parse, always showNotification a fallback); adopt Declarative Web Push on 18.4+ devices to eliminate the penalty class entirely.

Agent uninstalls the PWA / clears Chrome data: endpoint starts returning 410 on next send → pruned; the ladder's later rungs (WhatsApp, backup agent) still fire, so no ticket is stranded by a dead device.
push.recommendation: PRIMARY = WhatsApp template to the agent's escalation phone; web push = the second channel, not the must-ping backbone. Reasoning for THIS use case (field agents, must-ping, quick answer): WhatsApp is a native app — delivery is Apple/Google-grade on both platforms with zero install friction, agents already live in it all day and have already allow-listed it in their Focus modes, and — decisive — WhatsApp's own notifications support NATIVE inline reply on both iOS and Android, so the founder's long-press-and-type dream already exists there today, whereas web push can never deliver it on iPhone (WebKit has no notification actions at all). The WhatsApp ticket template should carry the same 2-second header (buyer · language · property · question) plus a URL button to the composer; hand the sibling WhatsApp lane the pointer that Twilio's inbound webhook exposes the quoted-message context (OriginalRepliedMessageSid) so an agent quote-replying to the ticket message can BE the answer — that is the true dream interaction and it works on iPhone. Web push earns its keep as: (a) the desktop dashboard ping (agents at the office answer fastest there), (b) free re-pings on the ladder (WhatsApp utility templates cost per message; web push costs nothing), and (c) the Android inline-reply fast path for agents who install the PWA. BUILD ORDER: 1) ticket + Answer Composer page (needed by every channel — the deep-link target); 2) WhatsApp ticket template + ladder scheduler + answer relay; 3) web push v1: SW + manifest + subscription endpoints + fanout + prune + resolve-dismissal (desktop + Android + iOS basic); 4) Android inline reply action; 5) guided iOS install UX; 6) later, Declarative Web Push adoption for 18.4+ devices. Never tell agents web push replaces WhatsApp alerts, and never promise iPhone inline reply from the AIVENA app — be honest in onboarding: 'iPhone: tap the alert, the answer box is already open'.
push.build_cost: Honest v1 estimate on the existing Next.js/Vercel + Hono/Railway + Supabase stack: 5-7 working days for one build session. Breakdown: minimal PWA shell (manifest, icons, SW registration, standalone detection) 1d; VAPID keys + subscription endpoints + push_subscriptions table + resubscribe-on-open client logic 1d; send fanout with web-push lib + Urgency/TTL + 410 pruning + resolve-dismissal pushes 1d; re-notification ladder (needs a scheduler tick — reuse the existing API 30-min sweep pattern from calendar sync but at 1-min granularity, or Supabase pg_cron hitting a Hono endpoint; Vercel serverless cannot hold timers) 1d; Answer Composer page with all states + deep-link auth return 1-1.5d; Android inline-reply action + tokenized SW answer POST 0.5-1d; guided iOS install/permission UX 0.5d. Dependencies: web-push npm package (free, no vendor), one VAPID keypair in Railway env, a scheduler tick, and real-device testing on at least one iPhone (iOS 17/18) and one Android — iOS behavior cannot be verified in a simulator or desktop Safari. No paid services: web push itself is free on all platforms (APNs for Safari included, no Apple Developer account needed). It pulls the manifest/SW/install-UX slice of the separate PWA lane forward (~1.5d of that lane done early); offline/app-shell work remains untouched in the later lane. The WhatsApp-channel parts (template, quoted-reply ingestion) are outside this estimate — they belong to the WhatsApp lane but reuse the same composer and ladder.

cadence_tone.mechanism:
PART A core mechanism — the agent channel IS WhatsApp, and cancellation is fire-time-checked, never pre-scheduled. Instead of waiting for the PWA push lane, ticket pings are sent as WhatsApp messages from a dedicated "AIVENA Office" sender (a second number on the existing WABA — same infra as the already-designed escalation phone) to the agent's personal WhatsApp. This makes the phone genuinely ring/buzz with WhatsApp's own notification, and it delivers the founder's dream interaction for free: on both Android (direct reply) and iOS (long-press/haptic press on the notification), WhatsApp natively opens an inline reply field on the notification itself — the agent reads "Marta (German) · IC-28746 San Javier · is the price negotiable?" and types the answer without opening any app. The reply arrives as a normal inbound Twilio webhook, is matched to the ticket, classified as an answer, and Amanda relays it to the buyer in the buyer's language with attribution within seconds. The re-notification engine is a 1-minute worker in the Railway API sweeping a single source of truth (amanda_tickets.next_ping_at + status): every ping decision is made at fire time under a row lock, so when an agent answers, one guarded UPDATE (status='answered', next_ping_at=NULL, WHERE status still open) atomically kills every future ping — there are no queued sends anywhere to chase down (deliberately NOT using Twilio message scheduling). The cadence is a bounded escalation ladder (max 4 pings to the owner-agent, then it adds PEOPLE — backup agent, then owner — never infinite repeats to the same phone), business-hours-aware with an honest night rule, and every reminder carries new information (ticket age, live buyer state, next-rung warning) so no two pings ever read identical.

PART B core mechanism — the doctrine is split into aspiration (system prompt) and law (deterministic send path), exactly matching the existing Amanda build contract's "deterministic validators, compliance in the send path" architecture. The system prompt owns voice: warm, short by default, mirror the buyer's length and register, attribute office answers, never claim to be human. The deterministic layer owns everything the founder actually fears: a length linter and question-sentence counter on every draft, a banned-pattern lexicon (urgency/scarcity/guilt phrases, per language) that rejects and regenerates drafts, a cooldown clock in the send scheduler that physically refuses uninvited double-texts, a rejected-property filter on every suggestion payload, and a disengagement state machine in lead_state (active → cooling → dormant) whose counters — max ONE value-bearing re-engagement per cooling episode, max two per conversation lifetime, then a graceful sign-off and silence — are enforced by the scheduler, not hoped for from the model. Disengagement itself is detected by a deterministic score (latency ratio vs the buyer's own median, reply-length collapse, closure tokens, read-no-reply), and a re-engagement may only fire if it carries a concrete payload from a whitelist (new matching listing, price change, new photos, an answer to a stated interest) — no payload, no nudge. A golden transcript-replay suite asserts the doctrine holds under adversarial prompting.
details: A1 — Channel: dedicated 'AIVENA Office' WhatsApp sender (second number on the existing WABA, or reuse the designed escalation-phone number) so the ops thread is visually distinct from buyer traffic; agent phone numbers collected at onboarding with a staff-privacy note. No PWA dependency — Web Push on iOS only works for installed home-screen PWAs and is far less reliable than a WhatsApp notification for this audience.

A2 — Notification anatomy: template line 1 is front-loaded to survive the ~60-char notification preview: '{lead_name} ({language}) · {property_ref} {short_location} · {question_gist}'. Body: the verbatim question, buyer state ('in the chat right now' for hot tickets), and one instruction line: 'Reply to this message with the answer — Amanda sends it to the client in their language. Reply SNOOZE 1h to snooze.' Optional Twilio quick-reply buttons: [Snooze 1h] [Pass to office]. Agent-facing templates only need Spanish + English (2-3 langs), not 13.

A3 — Reply→ticket matching, in order: (1) Twilio's OriginalRepliedMessageSid when the agent swipe-replies on the question inside the chat (deterministic); (2) inline notification replies carry NO quote context — so if the agent has exactly one open ticket, bind to it; (3) otherwise Amanda instantly sends a numbered list ('Which one? Reply like "2: yes, down to 240"') and a #N / 'N:' prefix parser resolves it.

A4 — Answer pipeline: intent-classify every agent reply {answer | snooze | pass | question-back | correction | noise}; only 'answer' relays. When the classifier is unsure, one-tap confirm buttons ('Send to client' / 'Discard') — friction only on ambiguity, never on clear answers. Amanda rewrites the raw answer into the buyer's language, warm and attributed ('I checked with the office — they say there is some room on price'), with a faithfulness constraint: the relay may not contain facts absent from the agent's text; raw + translated both stored for audit. Relay target ≤60s after the agent's reply. Agent then receives a confirmation preview ('Sent to Marta in German: …'), which also catches mistranslations.

A5 — Priority tiers (deterministic): P1 HOT = buyer messaged within last 15 min, OR blocking question type (offer/price-negotiation/viewing/availability), OR lead heat score high. P2 WARM = default. P3 CASUAL = cold lead / general info. Priority recomputes on every buyer inbound while the ticket is open — an upgrade pulls next_ping_at forward; never auto-downgrades mid-ticket except overnight.

A6 — Cadence ladder (all offsets in BUSINESS minutes vs agency_hours; default M–F 09:30–19:00 + Sat 10:00–14:00, per-agency config): P1: t0, +10m, +30m, +60m URGENT wording → backup agent at +60m (full-context ping + one +15m reminder) → owner at +2h → optional Twilio Voice TTS call rung at +90m (per-agency toggle; the only way to make a phone literally ring). P2: t0, +30m, +2h → backup at +4h → owner via next-morning digest. P3: low-key t0, +3h, then folds into next-morning digest only. Hard bound per ticket: ≤4 pings to the owning agent, ≤2 to backup, ≤1 to owner — escalation adds people, never repeats forever at one phone. Each rung uses a different template with new info (age, buyer live-state, 'last reminder before this goes to Miguel') so pings never read identical.

A7 — Night rule: t0 ALWAYS lands, even at 22:00 (a single message; many agents will answer from the sofa), but night-t0 wording appends 'the client has been told to expect an answer in the morning — no rush tonight'. Zero reminders during quiet hours 21:30–08:30 agency-local; unanswered tickets resume the ladder at opening+10m at the rung they were on. A reminder that would land within 15 min of closing shifts to next opening (P1 excepted, hard stop 21:30).

A8 — Anti-spam guards: per-agent cap 6 ticket pushes/hour and 20/day, overflow auto-switches to digest mode; with ≥3 open tickets for one agent, individual reminders collapse into ONE numbered digest per tick (new P1 t0 pings stay individual); snooze parser accepts '1h' / '30m' / 'snooze' → moves next_ping_at and acks 'I'll remind you at 16:30 — the client knows we're on it'; snooze caps: P1 one 30m snooze then the ping offers 'or reply PASS to hand it to {backup}', P2/P3 max two snoozes.

A9 — Cost note (true as of 2025–2026 Meta per-message pricing): t0 outside an open window is a paid utility template (a few cents); the moment the agent replies anything, a 24h customer-service window opens and all subsequent reminders, digests and confirmations are free-form session messages at no per-message template cost; utility templates sent inside an open window are free.

A10 — Atomic cancellation (the stated requirement, designed exactly so): NO pre-scheduled sends anywhere. Single source of truth = amanda_tickets (status, priority, rung, next_ping_at). A 1-minute worker in the existing Railway API selects due rows FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, re-checks status='open' UNDER the lock, sends, then writes the next rung + next_ping_at. Answering executes UPDATE amanda_tickets SET status='answered', answered_at=now(), next_ping_at=NULL WHERE id=$1 AND status IN ('open','escalated') RETURNING * — one statement kills every future ping and simultaneously guards the two-agents race (0 rows returned = someone answered first; the loser is told 'Already answered by María — she said: …'). Worst-case race is one benign extra ping mid-send, self-healed next tick.

A11 — Buyer-facing wait policy (honest, calm, bounded): at filing during open hours: 'Good question — I'll check with the office and come back to you. Shouldn't take long.' At filing when closed: '…they've closed for today, so I'll have your answer tomorrow morning.' Exactly ONE proactive wait-update per ticket, fired only when the implied window is blown (P1 ~50 min; P2 ~3h business; P3 next business day noon), only in buyer-daytime hours, and it MUST carry value ('Still waiting on the office — meanwhile, this just came up two streets away: …'); never a bare 'still waiting…', never a second update. Answer delivery is always attributed; 'thanks for your patience' added only when it was actually slow.
A12 — Never silent-drop: at 3 business days unanswered the ticket expires into a human-handoff dashboard task and Amanda tells the buyer honestly that {named agent} will contact them directly.

A13 — SLA metrics: amanda_tickets stores created_at, priority, first_ping_at, delivered_at/read_at (Twilio status callbacks; 'read' only when the agent's receipts are on), answered_at, answer_relayed_at, answered_by, pings_sent, rung_reached, snooze_count, wait_update_sent, expired; ticket_events is an append-only audit (every ping/snooze/escalation/relay incl. raw agent text + translated relay). Derived: business-minutes-to-answer (fair across overnights) and relay latency. Dashboard: per-agency median + p90 business-time-to-answer, % answered <15 min, escalation rate; per-agent view framed as coaching (public leaderboard = founder's call). Later trust stat: 'buyer questions answered in a median of X minutes'. Undelivered/failed status callbacks also feed the ladder: undelivered → skip that agent's remaining rungs immediately.

B1 — Length law: default ≤3 sentences AND ≤35 words, one idea per bubble. Mirroring: rolling median of the buyer's last 5 message lengths sets Amanda's target band (0.7–1.5×, floor = one short sentence); register mirroring too (tu/usted, emoji use, formality). Long-form allowed (≤120 words / ~700 chars, preferably split into two bubbles) ONLY when: the buyer asked a broad open question; it is the one re-engagement message; a requested property summary; or an office-answer relay needing context. Never two long messages in a row — the linter enforces all of this on every draft.

B2 — Question discipline: max ONE interrogative sentence per message (linter counts question sentences, not '?' characters). Question budget: after two consecutive Amanda questions the buyer answered, the next message must be statement-only. Intel slots (budget, timeline, financing, purpose, current situation) live in lead_profile; one natural follow-up only when contextually earned; a filled slot is never re-asked (deterministic blocker); enumerating multiple slots in one message is a banned form — intel is a slow drip across the conversation, never a form.

B3 — Disengagement score (deterministic, per turn): latency signal (current gap >3× the buyer's own median gap AND >8h), brevity collapse (last 2 replies ≤3 words after a longer baseline), per-language closure tokens ('ok', 'vale', 'thanks', 'we'll see', thumbs-up-only), a declined suggestion with no counter-ask, and read-no-reply ≥24h where read receipts exist. Threshold crossing flips lead_state active → cooling.

B4 — Re-engagement: cooling triggers exactly ONE nudge, ≥24h after the buyer's last message, sent at 11:00 or 18:00 local, and it may only fire with a concrete payload from a whitelist: new matching listing, price change, new photos/video, or an answer to something the buyer earlier said they cared about. No payload available = no nudge (hold up to 7 days waiting for an event). No reply within 5–7 days → one graceful sign-off ('I'll leave you in peace — I'm here whenever you like, and I'll only write if something truly matching appears') → state=dormant, all proactive contact stops. Lifetime cap: max 2 value-nudges per conversation EVER, counted in lead_state and enforced by the scheduler. Consented property-alerts are a separate opt-in stream (≤1/week) exempt from the cap.

B5 — Pushiness guardrails: the send scheduler refuses any uninvited message within 20 min of Amanda's last outbound (exceptions: delivering the promised office answer, correcting an error, finishing a deliberately split message). rejected_property_ids in lead state filters every suggestion payload — a rejected property can never be re-pitched. Banned-pattern lexicon per language (urgency/scarcity: 'last chance', 'won't last', 'many interested buyers', 'act now'; guilt: 'you haven't replied'; fake deadlines) runs as regex + phrase matching in the send path: fail → regenerate with feedback, 2 retries → human queue.

B6 — Human proximity: Amanda references the real office naturally and truthfully ('I'll check with the office', 'María can show it Saturday' — real names, real facts only), hands over with a named agent, never claims to be human, and never denies being an AI assistant when asked (existing honesty guard). Pacing: 20–90s jittered send delay scaled to reply length — never an instant wall of text.

B7 — Enforcement split, explicit: system prompt = voice, warmth, mirroring guidance, attribution phrasing, when-longer-is-ok. Deterministic send path = length linter, question-sentence counter, banned-pattern lexicon, cooldown clock, night-hours gate, re-engagement counter + active/cooling/dormant state machine, rejected-property filter, filled-slot re-ask blocker. The prompt is aspiration; the validators are law — the model can draft whatever it likes, but nothing leaves the send path that violates the doctrine.

B8 — Golden suite (transcript-replay assertions, extends the existing test harness): (i) buyer silent after 3 messages → exactly one payload-bearing nudge ≥24h later, then silence; (ii) 'ok'-only buyer → Amanda's messages shorten and questions stop; (iii) broad area question → long reply passes the linter's exception; (iv) rejected property never reappears across a 50-turn fuzz; (v) two-question draft → rejected and regenerated to one; (vi) 22:00 ticket → buyer gets the closed-office line, no wait-update before morning, agent t0 carries no-rush wording, reminders start 08:40; (vii) adversarial urgency injection → banned-pattern block holds; (viii) simulated scheduler race → one send, not two; (ix) hot ticket answered in 3 min → attributed relay ≤60s; (x) two agents answer simultaneously → single relay, loser notified with the winning answer.
edge_cases: Two agents answer the same ticket simultaneously → guarded UPDATE (WHERE status still open) means exactly one wins; the second gets 0 rows and receives 'Already answered by {name} — the client was told: …'. Never two relays to the buyer.

Agent inline-replies from the notification while holding multiple open tickets → inline replies carry no WhatsApp quote context, so Amanda immediately sends a numbered disambiguation list; '2: yes, negotiable' prefix parser resolves; swipe-reply inside the chat resolves deterministically via OriginalRepliedMessageSid.

Answer arrives after the buyer's 24h WhatsApp session closed → relay goes out via a pre-approved 13-language utility template answer_relay_v1 ('Hello {{name}}, about {{property}}: I checked with the office — {{answer}}'). Submit this template to Meta on day 1 — approval is the long pole.

Ticket filed at 22:00 → t0 still lands (with 'no rush tonight — client expects an answer in the morning'), buyer is told 'tomorrow morning', zero re-pings until 08:30, ladder resumes at opening+10m at its current rung.

Agent's WhatsApp unreachable (Twilio 'undelivered'/'failed' status callback) → skip that agent's remaining rungs, escalate to the next person immediately, raise an admin alert; cadence never stalls on a dead phone.

Agent reply is not an answer ('who??', 'call me', a question back) → intent classifier stops the relay; Amanda clarifies with the agent or converts to a handoff task; raw agent text is never forwarded to a buyer without passing answer classification.

Question becomes moot mid-wait (buyer moves on, or the property is sold/withdrawn) → ticket auto-cancels (status='cancelled_moot'); the agent gets one courtesy note only if already pinged; if the property is gone, Amanda tells the buyer and pivots to alternatives.
Duplicate question (same lead + property + semantically same question while a ticket is open) → dedupe onto the existing ticket; no second ping is ever generated.

Agent corrects themselves after the relay already went out (follow-up message within 10 min on the same ticket) → correction flow: Amanda sends the buyer a transparent 'small correction from the office — …'; both versions logged in ticket_events.

Single-agent agency (no backup) → ladder collapses to agent → owner → optional voice-call rung; onboarding validation requires at least one fallback contact before amanda_question tickets can be enabled.

Agent off-duty / on vacation → per-agent on_duty flag + simple duty roster; tickets route to the on-duty agent; nobody on duty behaves exactly like closed-hours (honest buyer expectation, t0 held for opening).

Mistranslation / unfaithful relay risk → agent receives a confirmation preview of the translated relay; the relay is constrained to add no facts beyond the agent's text; raw + translated stored side-by-side for audit.

Buyer keeps chatting while the ticket is open → Amanda keeps engaging normally (other Q&A, alternatives, natural intel) and priority recomputes on every inbound — a P2 ticket upgrades to P1 and next_ping_at is pulled forward.
Snooze abuse → hard caps (P1: one 30m snooze then a PASS offer; P2/P3: two), snoozes logged and visible in the agency SLA metrics.

Read-receipt asymmetry → 'read' timestamps exist only when the agent has receipts enabled; cadence logic never depends on read status (and reminders never say 'you read this' — creepy); only delivery FAILURE changes the ladder.
cadence_tone.recommendation: Build order: (1) The atomic core — amanda_tickets + ticket_events schema, the 1-minute fire-time-checked worker in the Railway API, t0 ping, answer webhook with the guarded UPDATE, and the attributed relay. This alone delivers the founder's headline promise (phone pings, long-press answer, buyer answered in their language in seconds). (2) Agent-side ergonomics — Spanish/English agent templates, inline-reply ticket matching + disambiguation, snooze/PASS parsers, answer confirmation preview. (3) The cadence ladder — priority tiers, business-hours arithmetic, night rule, escalation to backup/owner, digests and anti-spam caps. (4) Buyer wait-policy lines + the answer_relay_v1 template in 13 languages — submit to Meta for approval on day 1 of the build, it is the external long pole. (5) SLA metrics + the dashboard stat. (6) Part B lands as validators inside the already-designed Amanda send-path (length linter, question counter, banned lexicon, cooldown clock, disengagement state machine, rejected-property filter) plus the golden suite — it is an increment on the red-team-hardened build contract, not a new system. Leave the Twilio Voice call rung and any per-agent leaderboard visibility for last (the leaderboard is a founder product call). Ship Part A under the drafts-only dial first: pings and agent answers are real from day one, but the buyer-facing relay passes the existing approval gate until the agency graduates to assisted mode — the ticket system then becomes the fastest path to trusting full auto, because every relay is a human-authored fact.
cadence_tone.build_cost: Part A core (schema, 1-minute worker, agent webhook + parsers, t0/answer/relay loop, cadence ladder, digests): roughly 1.5–2 weeks of focused build on the existing Hono/Railway + Supabase stack — no new infrastructure, the worker pattern and Twilio inbound handling already exist (calendar sweeps, escalation-phone design). External dependencies and their lead times: Meta approval of answer_relay_v1 in 13 languages plus 4–5 agent-facing templates in 2 languages (days; submit day 1), a second WhatsApp sender on the existing WABA (or reuse of the escalation number — zero cost), per-agency configuration collected at onboarding (agency hours, backup agent phone, owner phone, agent numbers with a staff-privacy note), and Twilio status callbacks enabled for delivered/read/failed. Running cost is negligible: only out-of-window t0 pings and out-of-window buyer relays are paid utility messages (cents each); everything after an agent's first reply rides the free 24h session. Part B is 3–5 days incremental because the validator send-path and graduated dial are already designed in the Amanda build contract — the new work is the specific linters/lexicons/state-machine columns and the golden transcript suite (extends the existing test harness). The Twilio Voice escalation rung is ~1 day extra and optional. Nothing here needs the PWA lane, a native app, or any platform capability that does not exist today — the long-press quick-answer is native WhatsApp notification behavior on both Android and iOS.

critical_flaws: push-reality overstates Chrome desktop inline reply: chromestatus confirms 'Enabled by default' (Android 68, Desktop 75) but the platform list is Android/Windows 10+/ChromeOS only and the NotificationAction type:'text' API is non-standard and absent from MDN and every other browser — an agent or office machine on macOS Chrome/Safari/Firefox silently gets no inline reply, so it must be a feature-detected progressive enhancement proven on real devices, never a design pillar.

cadence-and-tone's night rule ('t0 ALWAYS lands, even at 22:00' to the agent's personal WhatsApp) collides with Spain's statutory right to digital disconnection (LOPDGDD Art. 88) for employed agents — the agency as employer takes on labor-law exposure, and this directly contradicts wa-reply-channel's queue-until-09:00 rule, so the night policy is both legally risky and internally inconsistent.

Wrong-buyer relay path: short-code recycling (Q1–Q9 reused after close) plus the single-open-ticket binding rule means an agent replying late to a stale, muted, or already-answered notification can have the answer bound to a DIFFERENT ticket and auto-relayed to the wrong buyer within 60 seconds — the confirmation echo arrives only after the damage is done; require a fresh-t0 recency check or explicit short-code before any auto-relay, and never recycle codes within the 7-day quote-context window.

The confirmation echo is shown in the BUYER's language ('Amanda is telling María in Norwegian: ...') which the Spanish agent cannot read, so the claimed mistranslation-catching safety mechanism in both wa-reply-channel and cadence-and-tone is illusory — the echo must be a back-translation into the agent's language (with the original stored for audit) or the faithfulness guarantee has no human check at all.

GDPR gap all three underplay: the relayed payload lands in the agent's CONSUMER WhatsApp — outside the WABA/Twilio DPA chain, backed up to the agent's personal iCloud/Google account, and unerasable when the agent leaves the agency — and 'first name only' does not sanitize the verbatim question text, which can carry arbitrary buyer PII (phone numbers, financial/personal circumstances); the minimal-payload option (property ref + question gist, no name, full context only behind the authenticated composer link) plus an offboarding/erasure policy must be a first-class design mode, not a footnote for legal review.

No design detects a muted agent thread: WhatsApp mute still returns 'delivered' status callbacks, so an annoyed agent who mutes the AIVENA Office chat (the predictable response to a 4-ping ladder) silently kills the entire channel while every SLA metric shows healthy delivery — the ladder needs a responsiveness signal (no reply to N consecutive t0s => treat as unreachable and escalate) independent of delivery status.
important_gaps: Small-agency reality: in a 2-person agency backup=owner=the same phone, so the escalation ladder's ≤4+≤2+≤1 caps collapse into up to 7 pings to one person, and cadence's onboarding rule 'require at least one fallback contact before tickets can be enabled' would lock solo agents out of the feature entirely — define an explicit solo/duo ladder profile.

No vacation/August mode: cadence's on_duty roster will not be maintained by a 2-person shop, and during Spain's normal August closure tickets expire silently at 3 days after buyers were told 'shouldn't take long' — need an agency-level away mode with honest buyer wording and suppressed SLA penalties.

Agents will CALL the buyer instead of typing: the ticket keeps re-pinging and escalates to a backup while the question is actually being handled by phone — cadence-and-tone has no zero-typing claim action at all (wa-reply's [Take over chat] button partially covers it); a one-tap 'I've got it' must exist on every ping in whichever design ships.

Backup-agent escalation relays answers from someone who may not know the property or lead, and first-answer-wins can ship the less-informed answer to the buyer with full office authority — escalated tickets should default to claim-then-answer or route to handoff rather than blind relay.

Shared-office-phone reality: many Spanish agencies run one office WhatsApp number for all staff, which breaks the single-open-ticket assumption that makes bare inline replies 'just work' — the dream interaction degrades to constant disambiguation menus; enrollment UX must push personal numbers or set expectations.

If the same personal number is both an enrolled staff number and the pre-existing escalation phone, one ticket generates duplicate templates to the same device (t0 plus escalation rung, plus web push if the PWA is installed on Android) — push-reality's channel matrix addresses this only for web push, not for the two WhatsApp-side sources.

The per-language banned-pattern regex lexicon across 13 languages is unmaintainable and misses inflections/idioms in Norwegian, Polish, Finnish etc., giving false confidence that pushy phrasing is blocked — needs an LLM-judge tier or a much smaller language set at launch.

Buyer-experience failure scenario the doctrine still permits: a buyer with a pending price question receives the single wait-update as a value-payload pitch for a DIFFERENT property ('meanwhile, this just came up two streets away') — deflection-plus-upsell while their question is unanswered is exactly the pushy feel the founder fears; wait-updates on open tickets should be status-honest, not sales-bearing.

Repetitive attribution becomes a robotic tic: with multiple tickets per conversation every relay opens 'I checked with the office —', a fixed phrase the buyer sees three times in an afternoon; the attribution requirement needs phrasing variation in the prompt layer.

The utility categorization of a staff-notification template is plausible but not guaranteed — Meta can recategorize templates at approval or later, and only wa-reply-channel plans quality/category monitoring; make that monitoring shared infrastructure.

Meta per-message pricing claims (free utility inside an open service window since July 2025, ~€0.02–0.04 Spain utility) are consistent across designs and directionally right but were not independently re-verified here — keep the designs' own 'verify rate card at build time' caveat in the doc.
conflicts_between_designs: Sender identity conflict: wa-reply-channel sends staff pings from the SAME agency number buyers chat with (webhook segregation carries the safety burden), while cadence-and-tone mandates a dedicated second 'AIVENA Office' sender — pick one; the dedicated sender is safer (staff replies can never race the lead pipeline) at the cost of a second number setup.

Night t0 contradiction: wa-reply-channel queues all pings outside 09:00–21:00, cadence-and-tone always delivers t0 even at 22:00 with no-rush wording — mutually exclusive policies on the exact same event.

Quiet-hours windows differ (09:00–21:00 vs 08:30/21:30 business-minutes arithmetic) and wa-reply's flat T0/+10/+30/+60 ladder conflicts with cadence's per-priority P1/P2/P3 ladders and push-reality's T0/+3/+10/+20/+40 ladder — three cadences for one requirement; if the WhatsApp ladder and the web-push ladder both run, the agent gets interleaved double pings unless push-reality's channel matrix (WhatsApp=phone, push=desktop) is adopted as the global rule.

Command grammar conflict: LATER=2h snooze vs SNOOZE 1h, 'Q3:'/'#3' prefixes vs '2:' prefixes, CALL/ME vs PASS — agents cannot learn two vocabularies; one merged reserved-word set (with Spanish synonyms) must be canonical.

Duplicate data models and schedulers: amanda_questions+amanda_question_notifications (wa-reply) vs amanda_tickets+ticket_events (cadence) describe the same entity, and each design specs its own 1-minute worker — build cadence's fire-time-checked atomic scheduler once with wa-reply's SID-indexed notification log folded in.

Escalation timing conflict: wa-reply escalates to the next staff number at a flat +30min, cadence escalates P1 at +60min and P2 at +4h — the flat rule would page a backup for casual questions that cadence deliberately keeps low-key.

Interaction-model tension: push-reality's recommended WhatsApp template carries a URL button to the composer while wa-reply's whole thesis is reply-in-thread — offering both 'tap to open dashboard' and 'reply to answer' on one notification dilutes the single-instruction clarity the 2-second rule depends on.
review.verdict: Adopt the WhatsApp-native channel as the backbone — its load-bearing platform claims verified (OriginalRepliedMessageSid with 7-day limit incl. quick-reply taps; native WhatsApp inline reply on both iOS and Android; list-picker session-only; iOS web push cannot do actions/inline reply) — but merge it with cadence-and-tone's superior atomic fire-time scheduler, priority tiers, and Part B validator doctrine, and accept push-reality's own recommendation of web push as desktop-plus-free-re-ping secondary (its Android inline-reply pillar is real per chromestatus but non-standard and platform-narrower than claimed, so demote it to feature-detected enhancement). Before writing the design doc, resolve: (1) dedicated second WhatsApp sender, not the buyer number; (2) ONE unified ladder, quiet-hours window (aligned with Spanish digital-disconnection law — no forced 22:00 pings to employees), and command grammar; (3) back-translated confirmation echo; (4) no auto-relay on ambiguous binding — short-code or fresh single-ticket only, and no short-code recycling inside 7 days; (5) minimal-payload GDPR mode (no buyer name, gist not verbatim, full context behind the authed composer) plus an agent-offboarding erasure note in the DPA lane; (6) mute-resilient liveness (unresponsiveness escalates even when delivery says OK); (7) solo/duo-agency ladder profile and a vacation mode. With those fixes this is a coherent, buildable ~2-3-week v1 on existing infrastructure.
